messages:
sre-incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU inference pool 'g4-prod' at 100% capacity; queue length spiking. Autoscaler not increasing replicas. Investigate now.

ash (oncall-sre): paging. I see throttling and lots of throttled requests in the queue graph. HPA metrics look stale. tagging @oncall-ml @maria for adapter/metrics path.

oncall-ml: looking. PromQL shows `sum(rate(gpu_inference_queue_length[1m])) by (pool) >> baseline`. promoter-adapter metrics show long scrape latency. Could be adapter -> prometheus relabel or metrics-server backlog.

maria (eng-runtime): on my side, runtime is healthy; 0 OOMs. We do see many pending requests with error code 429 from the api-proxy. Could be autoscaler not seeing cpu/memory/custom_metric updates.

ash (oncall-sre): copying useful commands:
```
# check HPA
kubectl -n inference get hpa g4-pool -o yaml
# check adapter logs
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/custom-metrics-adapter -c adapter --since=10m
# prometheus query
rate(custom/gpu_queue_length[1m])
```

oncall-ml: adapter logs show repeated 503s to prometheus: `GET /api/v1/query?query=... 503 connection timeout` and backlog warnings. metrics-server shows `queued 1200 samples` in logs.

ash (oncall-sre): that explains it — HPA uses custom metrics via adapter which can't query prometheus -> HPA not scaling. For immediate mitigation we can: 1) manually scale HPA/Deployment to add capacity, 2) re-route some traffic to smaller models / failover region, 3) restart custom-metrics-adapter if it's flapping. Thoughts?

maria (eng-runtime): recommend manual scale first to relieve customer impact, then debug adapter. I can push a temporary scale to replicas=12 for g4 pool.

kevin (cs): FYI a customer (acme-analytics) reported increased latency and 429s around 11:07 UTC. They're on Dedicated with pinned g4 pool. They want ETA.

ash (oncall-sre): actioning manual scale now. `kubectl -n inference scale deployment g4-worker --replicas=12` -> done. Queue length falling? monitoring -> queue length drops ~70% within 2m. API 429s decrease.

devops-bot: deploy-check: horizontal-pod-autoscaler/g4-pool still reports desired=6 current=6 (no change). Manual scale applied to deployment.

oncall-ml: while we apply mitigation, I'll restart adapter to re-establish metrics path. Doing `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/custom-metrics-adapter`.

maria (eng-runtime): adapter restart logs show improved connectivity — queries returning 200. metrics-server backlog draining. HPA custom metrics now available: `kubectl get --raw "/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1"` shows gpumetrics.

ash (oncall-sre): good. Monitor HPA: `kubectl -n inference describe hpa g4-pool` -> it now reports external metric received and desired replicas -> should auto-adjust down.

kevin (cs): telling acme-analytics we’ve mitigated and are investigating root cause. ETA for full RCA?

ash (oncall-sre): immediate impact mitigated via manual scaling + adapter restart. Next steps: collect adapter/prome logs, spot whether Prometheus ingestion spike or network blip caused timeouts. Raising incident to P1 page for RCA. Assigning to @maria and @oncall-ml.

maria (eng-runtime): initial logs show Prometheus had a scrape backlog at 11:05 UTC due to heavy cardinality from a recent canary test that generated many label values. We're paginating alerting queries concurrently which increased scrape latency. We'll correlate recent deployments.

oncall-ml: also saw a surge of requests with long sequences from a batch job between 11:04-11:06 causing queue spike. Frequency combined with scrape backlog tipped HPA into blind mode.

taylor (prod): customer-impact summary for postmortem: multiple customers on g4 pool experienced 10–30s tail latency and 429 throttles for ~6 minutes; no data loss; manual scale and adapter restart restored normal behavior. Estimated affected requests: ~14k.

kevin (cs): sent initial status to affected customers: short degradation, engineering mitigation applied, further updates after RCA.

maria (eng-runtime): mitigation follow-ups: 1) throttle or sandbox high-cardinality canary metrics to not hit Prometheus, 2) add circuit-breaker in adapter to fail fast vs Prometheus if timeouts exceed threshold, 3) implement cache for external metric queries for short windows.

oncall-ml: ops follow-ups: increase HPA metric scrape timeout and add alerting for `adapter_scrape_latency` and `metrics_server_queue_length` crossing thresholds. Also create runbook steps for manual scale + adapter restart.

ash (oncall-sre): handoff: my on-call shift ends in 40m. @maria, @oncall-ml please own RCA and rollback plan if we need to tighten cardinality controls. I'll add a short summary to #incidents and mark P1 -> investigating.

maria (eng-runtime): taking lead on RCA. I'll collect logs and add timeline to the incident doc.

oncall-ml: I'll own mitigations + follow-up alerts.

kevin (cs): I'll coordinate customer comms and follow up with impacted accounts.

devops-bot: reminder: create incident ticket INC-2311-045 in PagerDuty and attach this thread.

ash (oncall-sre): closing loop for now — monitoring for 30m. If queue spikes again, escalate to emergency scale and route traffic to eu-west as fallback.

maria (eng-runtime): note for RCA: likely root cause = Prometheus scrape backlog due to high-cardinality canary + concurrent long-running evals; adapter timed out -> HPA blind -> capacity exhausted. Proposed long-term fixes: metric cardinality guardrails, adapter caching, synthetic HPA fallback to CPU when external metrics absent.

oncall-ml: adding PR references for fixes. Will schedule a postmortem doc with timeline and actionable owners.

kevin (cs): customers updated. No escalations so far.

ash (oncall-sre): final status at handoff: service stabilized, manual scale reverted to autoscaled desired when HPA healed; assigning follow-ups to eng-runtime and eng-ml. I'll sign off from on-call. :white_check_mark:
